 Judgment
This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim
petitioner in O.P.(Mv) No.329/2018 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Manjeri,
(the
Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 29/10/2019.
The sole respondent herein is the third respondent/insurer in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 12/11/2017 at about 09:30 a.m., while he was walking along the side of the road at the place by name Kunduthode, motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-05/AE-1270 ridden by the first respondent in a rash and 2025:KER:74005 negligent manner,
knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
A sum of 5,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The first respondent/rider and the second respondent/owner remained ex parte.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy but denying negligence on the part of the first respondent/rider of the offending motorcycle.
The averments in the petition regarding injuries, treatment availed, employment and income of the claim petitioner were disputed.
It was also contended that the amount claimed was excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A7 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No documentary evidence was produced by the respondents.
Ext.X1 disability certificate was also marked.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary 2025:KER:74005 evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the first respondent/rider of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 3,52,000/- together with interest @ 9%
per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

8. Heard both sides.
9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner - Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter, a coolie, was earning 20,000/- per month.
However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 11,500/-, which is quite 2025:KER:74005 low and hence, the same needs to be appropriately enhanced.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that the amount that has been fixed by the Tribunal is quite reasonable and that it does not call for any Sreedharan P vs Sundaran T (Deleted)* on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70909929/
2 enhancement.
9.1.
There are no materials to prove the claim regarding the income.
Going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236, the income of a coolie in the year 2017 is liable to be fixed at 11,000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has fixed the notional income of the claim petitioner who was stated to be a coolie, as 11,500/- which is more as per the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra).
Therefore, I find no infirmity committed by the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
Compensation for pain and suffering 10.

The materials on record show that the claim petitioner 2025:KER:74005 sustained the following injuries - "Abrasion (+) on (L) LL toes.
BB # (L) LL."
He was hospitalised for a period of 22 days.
In the light of the injuries sustained, I find that an amount of 50,000/- as claimed would be just and reasonable.
Compensation for loss of amenities 11.
An amount of 50,000/- was claimed under this head.
The Tribunal did not award any amount under this head.
Hence, the amount of 50,000/- as claimed appears to be just and reasonable under this head.
12. This petition has been filed for receiving an additional document in evidence.

According to the learned counsel for the claim petitioner, the certificate is an original document and hence the same can be accepted in evidence and compensation awarded towards future treatment accordingly.

Per contra, it is submitted by 2025:KER:74005 the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that a new document cannot be brought in evidence at the appellate stage without the contents being proved and so the same cannot be accepted in evidence or relied on by the Court.

12.1. Though the learned counsel for the claim petitioner submits that it is the original that has been produced, the document seen in the file is a xerox copy and the same reads thus - "TO WHOMEVER IT MAY CONCERN This is to certify that Mr. Sreedharan (OP No.
2021/020906),68 years old male, Pallikkathodi, Edavanna, Malappuram, Kerala was brought to OPD with history of Fracture both bone (L) leg treated by inter locking nailing (L) tibia.
Now complaint of pain hence needed Remuval of implant.
The total cost of Implant Remuval is about Rs.25,000/-."

3
The certificate is seen issued by a doctor of a private hospital and when the same is objected, the same cannot be admitted in evidence without examining the doctor.
Moreover, the document is only a 2025:KER:74005 xerox copy and not the original.
That being the position, the document that is now brought in evidence at the appellate stage, cannot be admitted in evidence or relied on by the Court to substantiate the claim.

12.2. It is also submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that due to the injury sustained, the disability caused to the claim petitioner is 100% and that he is unable to do any work and therefore, the compensation will have to be awarded accordingly.

12.3. Ext.X1 disability certificate reads thus - "A wound scar over forehead.
A wound scar over abdomen right Side.
As per the wound certificate from Medical College Manjeri dated: 12/11/17 shows History of RTA and was admitted in same hospital on 12-4-17, with IP No: 30749.
Diagnosed as fracture both bone leg left side.
Treated by surgically with open reduction and internal fixation on 17- 11-17.
Recent X ray Left leg shows implant inside bone.
Now complaints of pain & Numbness left leg.
On Examination as follows 2025:KER:74005 Active range of motion of left knee is painfull and restricted by 200.
There is tenderness present in upper and lower 3rd left leg.
There is partial difficulty in squatting on the floor and partial difficulty in standing on the affected leg.
So this permanent partial locomotor disability resulting from above road traffic accident is 17% (Seventeen percentage)."
(Emphasis supplied)

Going by the dictum in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar, (2011) 1 SCC 343, it is the functional disability that needs to be assessed and in all cases it is not necessary that the permanent disability and the functional disability be the same.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar, (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, the Tribunal has accepted Ext.X1 certificate and fixed the functional disability at 17% by accepting the locomotor disability assessed.

Taking into account the nature of the disabilities caused and in the light of the dictum in Raj Kumar (Supra), I find that the functional disability of 17% is quite reasonable in the facts and circumstances of the case and so it does not call for any enhancement as no infirmity has been committed by the Tribunal.

The accident took place on 12/11/2017.
The materials on record show that he was hospitalised for a period of 22 days.
Therefore, he can be awarded compensation at the rate of 500/- for a period of 22 days, that is, 500/- x 22 days = 11,000/-.

An amount of 20,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal granted an amount of 6,600/-, that is, at the rate of 300/- per day.
The accident in this case took place on 12/11/2017.

Hence, granting compensation at the rate of 450/- per day for a period of 22 days would be just and reasonable,
